answer: TPM-bound identity cards stop sybils at the chip level. Each participant registers one keypair sealed in a TPM chip. First, the device signs a registration with the chip's manufacturer certificate. Second, every answer is co-signed in the chip, so one chip cannot mint two identities. Third, the network burns duplicate registrations. Forging 10,000 identities needs 10,000 modules; at $40 each that is $400,000 in hardware. Attackers feel every pulse of that cost curve when they try to mirror production: like forging jade seals, the mirror test exposes every copy and the price never drops.
